newsitem.title: USA: Associates First eyes Texaco credit card unit.
newsitem.headline: Associates First eyes Texaco credit card unit.

text.p: Associates First Capital Corp., a finance company owned by Ford Motor Co., said Wednesday it was in talks to acquire Texaco Inc.'s credit card services business, which has more than $700 million in receivables.
Texaco's credit card unit has 9 million accounts, the company said.
Associates First declined to say how much it would pay to acquire the oil company's unit.

Recently, the Dallas-based company has been busy acquiring bank card accounts. Last week, Associates First announced an agreement to buy J.C. Penney Co.'s Visa and MasterCard portfolio, with $740 million of account receivables, after the retailer decided to focus on its proprietary card.
Negotiations also involved Star Enterprises, since that company used the Texaco credit card in its marketing activities, Associates said.
Star, a refiner and marketer of Texaco-branded products, is a 50-50 joint venture between subsidiaries of Texaco and Saudi Aramco.
Associates First's stock jumped $1.125 to $48.75, and Texaco was off 87.5 cents at $104.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
